steps: Locate the fireplace
Plan the unit, vent and gas line together; keep it out of traffic and hold the Figure 2 & 3 clearances. Fit the top standoffs (shipped loose inside) once the unit is on site and in position.

Install to the current CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes; only qualified (licensed or trained) personnel. In Massachusetts, only a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter may install it.

  • Possible locations: an existing wall, a corner, a built-in wall or a wall projection (Figure 8).
  • Keep it out of high-traffic areas and away from furniture and draperies.
  • Must not be connected to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.
  • Manufactured (mobile) home: allowed where local codes permit; the fireplace must be fastened in place.
  • Top standoffs ship loose inside the fireplace; install them on top once it is on site and in position (Figure 7).
Frame both faces
With the unit in place and the vent installed, fit the two supplied steel stud framing kits, one on each face. No combustible material, wiring, insulation, vapour barrier or gas plumbing inside them.

Two Steel Stud Framing Kits are supplied and must be used unless the fireplace is totally enclosed with non-combustible material. Both faces must be framed with them.

  1. Assemble each frame: header stud, two center studs, stud plate, inner and outer side studs, base plates (p. 13).
  2. Attach it to the unit framing brackets flat side out, the side without screw holes facing away from the fireplace.
  3. Secure it to existing framing through the horizontal top stud and the base plates.
  4. Sheet the front with non-combustible backer board (cement board or equivalent) using drywall screws.

The frames adjust for wall depths from 23 3/4" to 27 1/4". Do not insulate or use plastic vapour barrier within the framing kit; seal the chase at the ceiling level or between floors. A full header above the metal framing kit is highly recommended.
Facing & hearth
Recess only with non-combustible material and keep the door and screen free to move. A hearth isn't required; if you fit one, keep it no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace.

The lintel is fixed: position the fireplace so the front face of the lintel sets its final position, allowing for the facing thickness (1/2 inch calcium silicate board or rock facing). A 3/4" facing finishes flush with the front of the unit.

  • No building material may protrude past the framing edges attached to the fireplace.
  • The area between the lintel and the glass door frame must stay free of obstructions; the door, with trim fitted, must move freely.
  • Finishing must not stop the glass door opening in the event of ignition of excess gas buildup.
  • Painted wall above: discard the framing kit; use full sheets of calcium silicate board (or equivalent) and full-length metal studs.
  • Hearth: many floors (such as wood) may not tolerate the radiant heat, so a non-combustible hearth no more than 1" above the bottom of the fireplace is suggested. Thicker hearths interfere with the safety screen and door frame unless the fireplace is raised.

Recess depth: up to 4 1/2" in non-combustible material; deeper, to a maximum 12", only if the facing is moved away from the face of the unit and the window 1:1, top and sides (see Framing & facing).
Electrical & wall switch

Connect the 110 V supply in the junction box behind the right-side access panel. Run the supplied 40 ft cable to the wall switch, check its continuity before walling in, and load 4 AA batteries in the wall switch.

Fireplace110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A
Optional power vent kit115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A
Communication cable40 ft (supplied)
  1. Place the fireplace, remove the door, then the access panel on the right-hand side of the firebox.
  2. Connect the 110 V. AC supply to the wires inside the junction box (Figure 24).
  3. Attach the wall switch to the framing and route the supplied cable to it.
  4. Check continuity of each wire in the cable before it is plugged in and walled in.
  5. Plug one end into the wall control and the other into the interface board.
  6. Insert the 4 supplied AA batteries in the wall switch battery pack (the Owner's Manual says none if a power vent is used).
  7. Install the burner with the burner kit instructions, if not already done.
  8. Turn on gas and power, check for leaks, then move the wall control center button to ON: the igniter sparks, the pilot lights, then the main burner.

With home automation, the top cable runs wall switch to fireplace and the bottom cable wall switch to the automation system.
Set PV / NV mode
Set the interface-board switch to NV for natural venting or PV with a power vent. Turn off power and remove the backup batteries whenever you change it.

The PV / NV switch is on the interface board (Figure 30). NV: vented without a power vent. PV: power vent installed (follow the power vent kit instructions).

Reset when switching: turn off the electrical supply to the fireplace and remove the backup batteries when changing between PV and NV, so the module resets properly.

With a power vent, the vent restrictor must be fully open (p. 30).
Gas supply + pressure check
3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet with a union or flare fitting (no hard pipe) and a sediment trap within 6 feet. Leak-test, then verify pressures lit on the highest setting.

• Gas line access holes: top and left sides of the Control Box. Use the correct gas line diameter.
  • Sediment trap per the national fuel gas code, no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve.
  • Do not hard pipe to the valve: provide a union or flare fitting so the valve can be repaired or replaced.
  • Connect to the gas connector (Figure 25), turn on the gas and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  • System pressure tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); isolate it by closing its shut-off at or below 1/2 psig.
  • Turn off the gas before removing a test-port plug; verify pressures lit on the highest setting. The test procedure is in the Burner Installation Manual.
Reinstall the access panel and its gasket after conversion, installation or servicing. Leaving it off overheats the control system and causes premature failure.
Vent & terminate
Use only Town & Country vent components and termination kits. Screw and tape every joint and stay inside the rise/run chart, 68 feet total maximum.

• Termination kits only: 22270012 (wall) or 22270010 (roof). Optional power vents (22270003, 22270004 & 22270013) need different venting; see their manuals.
  • Join every component tightly with sheet metal screws and seal outer joints with the supplied high-temperature self-adhesive aluminium tape.
  • Wall: frame a 14 1/2" opening centred at least 61" above the floor; a wall thimble is required through a combustible wall (up to 12" thick). The terminal must not be recessed into the wall or siding; caulk it in place.
  • Roof: frame a 14 1/2" opening (larger as the roof pitch increases, table on p. 26), a ceiling firestop at each floor or ceiling, roof support bracket, flashing, storm collar sealed with mastic, then the cap. The pipe extends at least 12" above the roof, more per the roof pitch table (p. 28).
  • Horizontal runs rise 1/4" for every 1 ft toward the termination. Keep vent length and elbows to a minimum for best flame appearance.
Set the vent restrictor
It leaves the factory open. Set it from the restrictor chart for your vent height and run, then fine-tune by flame appearance; it must be fully open with a power vent.

The restrictor (secondary air adjustment) is on the underside of the firebox top. Determine the vent height and horizontal length, then read the position from the chart (Figure 45). The chart is a diagram, so read it from the page. Positions are based on lab tests; the ideal position may vary slightly.

  1. Loosen the screws holding the restrictor plates.
  2. Move the plates to the intended opening.
  3. Retighten the screws.

Too closed: flame excessively tall and lifting, lacks movement, soots. Too open: flame height low, excessive movement.

The vent restrictor must be fully open when using the power vent.
Panels, trim & screen
Install a firebox panel set before the burner media; never run the fireplace without panels. Then fit the transition trim and the magnetic safety barrier screen.

A Firebox Panel Set must be installed for safe operation. See the burner instructions first. Fibre panels may need trimming to fit, and all panels are very fragile.

  1. Remove the side panel retainers under the firebox heat shield (one screw each).
  2. Install the left and right front floor panels, then the left and right rear floor panels.
  3. Install the left side panel bottom first, angling it up into place (push the firebox shield up if needed), then the right side panel.
  4. Reinstall the panel retainers.

Transition trim kit (80002252), with the door in place: side pieces first (two small button magnets each), the top piece over them (two larger magnets), then the meshed bottom piece in the gap between the outer-most door frame and the glass, with the Town & Country badge on its right-hand side. Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer-most door frame.
Pair wall switch & remote
With the wall switch on Remote, hold its Program button up to 10 seconds to pair it to the fireplace; then press Program once and the remote's on/off button within 60 sec.

Wall switch to fireplace

  1. Set the wall switch selector to Remote.
  2. Press and hold the Program button (use a straightened paper clip) for up to 10 seconds; the wall switch beeps 5 times. Release.
  3. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then another 3: they are paired.

If a nearby fireplace responds instead, repeat to switch to another of the three available channels.

Remote to wall switch

  1. Press and release Program once; the wall switch beeps 3 times.
  2. Within 60 sec., press and release the on/off button on the remote; the wall switch beeps 3 times.

With the basic wall switch, the remote pairs directly to the module, which gives the beeps (p. 38).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself. An electronic igniter lights the pilot automatically, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you light it

Smell all around the fireplace for gas, including next to the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low. If you smell gas, don't light it (see Safety & gas smell).

  1. Turn it on with the On/Off switch on the wall switch, or the On/Off key on the remote.
  2. Give it a moment. It can take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you turn it on.
  3. Once the burner is lit, set the flame with the remote.
  4. If it doesn't light, switch it off and wait at least 5 minutes for any gas to clear. If you still smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety & gas smell. If you don't smell gas, try again.
  5. If it won't light or stay lit after several tries, switch it off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace, and call your service technician or gas supplier.
Very first start: it needs extra time while air escapes from the gas lines.

Turning it off

Switch it off at the wall switch or the remote. If it is going to be serviced or shut down for a long time, also turn off all electric power to it and remove the backup batteries.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
Your handset is a Proflame 2 transmitter with a blue backlit screen. It runs on 3 AAA batteries.

  • On/Off key: turns the fireplace on or off. A single beep from the fireplace confirms each command.
  • Up and down arrows: six flame levels. Down lowers the flame one step at a time until it is off; up raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, pressing up brings the flame back on high.
  • Mode key: steps through features. Go to the light bulb icon, then use the arrows to set the light through six levels.
  • Key lock: press Mode and up together to lock the keys against unsupervised use. A lock icon shows. Press both again to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together, then look for the F or C beside the room temperature.
Thermostat: the thermostat function is off by default. The manual says it is not permitted in the USA (it is in Canada). The manual describes this as a decorative fireplace, not a heating appliance.

If the remote's batteries are low or dead, turn the fireplace off with the On/Off switch on the wall switch.

sounds.title: That sound, smell or beep
sounds.html:
A smell the first few hours

The first time you light it, expect a slight odor for a couple of hours while paints, sealants and lubricants cure. It is temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room; the fumes can bother some people.

Ticking and popping

Steel expands and contracts as it heats up and cools down. Those noises are normal, much like the sounds a furnace or oven makes.

A short wait before it lights

It can take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you turn it on.

Beeps

  • One beep: the fireplace received your command.
  • A double beep when you use the remote: the backup batteries are low. Replace them and you will hear a single beep again.
A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch any electrical switch and don't use any phone in your building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone, or the fire department if you can't reach them.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it with a fireplace glass cleaner. Wipe the outside finish with mild soap and water.

  • Only clean the glass when it is cool, never when hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • Before any servicing, turn off the gas and electrical power and give it plenty of time to cool.

Cracked or broken glass

Don't strike or knock the glass. Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken. It must be replaced first, by a licensed or qualified service person. Use ceramic glass only, from your Town & Country dealer.

The seal matters. The glass gasket must stay in good condition; it is checked at the yearly inspection. Any door or panel removed for servicing must go back on before you use the fireplace.

app.title: Using the TC Fire app
app.html:
You can run the fireplace from a Bluetooth phone with the free TC Fire app, from the Apple App Store (iOS) or the Google Play Store (Android).

First the wall switch must be paired to the fireplace, and the remote to the wall switch (steps 1 and 2 in the manual). Then:

  1. Download TC Fire and open it.
  2. Go to Add/Edit Fireplace and press Add.
  3. Find the PIN on the sticker on your wall switch.
  4. Enter the PIN and a name for the fireplace, then press Save.

The fireplace now shows on the app's main screen. Toggle buttons turn the flame and the lights on and off; sliders raise and lower the flame and light levels.

You only see your saved fireplace when your phone is within Bluetooth range and no one else is controlling it.

pilot.title: Pilot mode: IPI or CPI
pilot.html:
The fireplace control can run the pilot in either of two modes:

  • IPI: intermittent pilot ignition
  • CPI: continuous pilot ignition

To change the mode

  1. Make sure the system is off.
  2. Press the Mode key until the CPI icon shows on the remote.
  3. Press the up arrow to turn on continuous pilot (CPI), or the down arrow to go back to IPI.
  4. A single beep confirms the change.

In either mode the igniter lights the pilot for you; never try to light it by hand. The pilot's flame size and operation are checked, and the pilot cleaned, at the yearly inspection.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power, with a battery pack as backup. The batteries are used only when house power is interrupted or lost.

Remote handset3 AAA
Wall switch battery pack4 AA
Power vent? If your fireplace uses a power vent, don't put batteries in the wall switch. The battery backup works only if the fireplace does not use a combustion fan.

Low batteries

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the power runs out, and goes away once you replace them.
  • Backup: the fireplace gives a double beep when it gets a command from the remote. After you replace them you will hear a single beep again.
  • Remote dead? Turn the fireplace off at the wall switch.

Turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace before you remove or reinsert batteries. For service or a long shutdown, turn off all electric power and take the backup batteries out.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
• Hot glass will burn. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • A barrier screen that reduces the risk of burns from the hot glass comes with the fireplace. It must be installed to protect children and other at-risk people.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. If anyone at risk lives with you, a physical barrier is recommended; an adjustable safety gate can keep toddlers out of the room.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies and anything flammable away. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors or liquids nearby.
  • Any panel or door removed for servicing must go back on before you use the fireplace.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

If you smell gas

  1. Don't try to light any appliance.
  2. Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  3. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions.
  4. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean more frequent cleaning. Don't try to repair it yourself; contact your dealer.

What the yearly inspection covers

  • Remove the glass and the decorative media (logs, pebbles or glass) and check for soot. Heavy soot means the fireplace should be inspected and adjusted for proper combustion. Clean the burner with a brush or vacuum, especially the burner ports.
  • Check the pilot for proper flame size and operation, and clean off soot and dust.
  • Check that the vent pipe and outside vent terminal are open and free of blockage.
  • Check the glass gasket and replace it if needed.
  • Check the batteries and replace them as needed.

Between visits, keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything combustible, and keep the burner and control compartment clean.

Town & Country recommends installers and technicians certified by the National Fireplace Institute (NFI) as NFI Gas Specialists.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
The Town & Country Limited Lifetime Warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only)Lifetime · parts only
Combustion chamberLifetime · parts only
Burner tube assemblyLifetime · parts only
Porcelain finishesLifetime · parts only
Any defective part2 years · parts and labor

The two years run from the original date of purchase.

Conditions

  • Installed by a qualified technician to local and national requirements and the appliance manual.
  • A sediment trap within 6 feet of the gas control valve.
  • The installer makes sure it fires as shown on the rating plate.
  • Some porcelain colors darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

Not covered

  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Installation, operating or environmental conditions beyond Town & Country's control.
Any installation or operation that departs from the manual voids the warranty. This is a summary; read the full terms.

The supply connects to the wires in the junction box in the right-side control compartment, behind the firebox access panel. Check continuity of the communication cable before walling it in. PV / NV switch on the interface board: NV for natural venting, PV with a power vent; turn off power and remove the backup batteries when changing it. For home automation, leave the wall switch on Remote; the control repeats the signal every 2 hours until a new command is received. With the basic wall switch, home automation is limited to flame on and off through a dry contact relay (solid brown wire and common).

index_extra.p: What to do if you smell gas
Wait 5 minutes, retry (if you still smell gas, stop), then call for service
One beep confirms; a double beep means low backup batteries
Off by default; not permitted in the USA
Mode and up together lock the remote's keys
Battery backup in the wall switch
Dry contact relay; 0 - 10 volt DC flame and light
Optional power vents need different venting

Non-combustible backer board side extension: 9 3/4" to the side of the framing edge bars (Framing and Finishing text) vs 10 1/4" to the sides (Figure 11).

review.notes: Input rates, efficiency (P.4.1-15: 36.3%), altitude and the certification standards appear only on the rating label (doc 1 p. 43); max 61,000 BTU/hr, efficiency and IPI/CPI ignition match the catalog; view_area (983 sq in) is not in either manual. The gas pressure test procedure and burner/media installation are in a separate Burner Installation Manual / burner kit instructions that are not part of this guide's sources. Shown only as diagrams and not transcribed: overall dimensions (doc 1 p. 5 Fig. 1), mantel clearance chart A-F (p. 5 Fig. 2), minimum combustible framing dimensions (p. 9 Fig. 10), roof-terminal clearances to adjacent structures (p. 28 Fig. 42), restrictor rise/run chart (p. 30 Fig. 45), vent offsets (p. 33) and wiring (p. 42). The rating label also lists 'Blower electrical rating: 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A' with no blower section anywhere else (kept in the Electrical drawer only) and the codes 'NH x2 or NE x1' / 'LH x2 or LE x1' with no explanation (left out). The owner's manual names IPI and CPI but does not say how they behave or which is the factory setting. The thermostat function is disabled by default and stated as not permissible in the USA; the Canadian enabling procedure (doc 2 p. 9) is deliberately not reproduced. The wall switch's 4 AA battery pack is treated as the backup battery pack (doc 1 p. 16 + doc 2 p. 7). Cross-reference slips in doc 1: p. 17 points to pages 38/39 for pairing (actually 37/38); the table of contents lists 'Lighting Instructions 37' but the installation manual has no lighting section (lighting is in doc 2 p. 4), and later TOC entries run one page early; p. 8 cites framing instructions on 'pages 10 & 11' (assembly is p. 13). The rating label shows 'SERIE: D' while the covers say Series D2 / 'D version 2'. The doc 2 p. 4 lighting label mentions a gas control knob that is not otherwise described for this unit; its warning (use only your hand, never use tools, force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion) is in the Safety drawer as printed. Massachusetts 248 CMR requirements (doc 1 p. 4) are not summarized.
